name: [R20] Burst of structured Markdown file writes from a single process across unrelated paths
message:
Exploratory heuristic for one of the three AI-involvement tells Unit 42 named in "An AI-Assisted Cyber Attack" (2026-09-02): structured Markdown files passed between agents/sessions to hand off information. Unit 42 gave no IOCs or filenames for this -- it was a forensic observation, not a published signature. This rule is this repository's own constructed proxy, not a confirmed indicator: a single process writing several distinct .md files across several distinct directories, outside known doc paths, in a short window -- a shape unusual for both normal human editing and most legitimate automation.

Treat every hit as a lead, not a confirmation. Correlate with this repo's other agentic-behavior signals (R1 LLM egress, R4 messaging C2, R5 persistence, R7 rapid multi-tool execution) before escalating -- Unit 42's own point is that AI involvement shows up as a *combination* of tells, not any single one. See unit42-ai-assisted-intrusion.ja.md section 7.

Tune: allowlist known doc-generation automation (changelog bots, static-site builders, monorepo doc-sync jobs) by process name/service account for your environment -- this threshold needs real baseline tuning before it's useful.

queries.name: md_write_event
queries.query: source:file_event @file.extension:md -@file.path:(*\/docs\/* OR *\/wiki\/* OR *\/.git\/* OR *README* OR *CHANGELOG* OR *node_modules\/* OR *site-packages\/*)

cases.name: Scattered Markdown writes from one process (needs SIEM-side distinct-directory + distinct-filename thresholds -- see rule message)
